t: G20 Fabrication Replication Engine: 3D-Print Budget Desk — Simple
name: G20 Fabrication Replication Engine: 3D-Print Budget Desk — Simple
title: G20 Fabrication Replication Engine: 3D-Print Budget Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Every print quoted before it starts: material = volume × density × (1 + support fraction), time = volume / volumetric rate. The desk computes both from the part's bounding volume and the process rate — no more surprise 40-hour prints.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Print time for 250 cm³ at 15 mm³/s = 4.63 hours. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

real_world_basis: Volumetric-rate budgeting is the real method used by print farms.
signature_version: Signature version: the UFR print desk — the chapter's synthesis target as the rate frontier, with the 'matter-energy' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: calibrate your printer's true volumetric rate, then budget every part before slicing.
math_note: Print time for 250 cm³ at 15 mm³/s: 4.63 hours [verified]; Fibonacci(20) — layer-count reference: 6765 layers [verified]

t: G20 Fabrication Replication Engine: CNC Feeds and Speeds — Simple
name: G20 Fabrication Replication Engine: CNC Feeds and Speeds — Simple
title: G20 Fabrication Replication Engine: CNC Feeds and Speeds — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] The machinist's arithmetic: spindle RPM = (surface speed × 1000) / (π × tool diameter), feed = RPM × flutes × chip load. The desk computes both from the material's surface speed — the difference between a clean cut and a broken tool.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: RPM for 300 m/min surface speed, 10 mm tool = 9549 RPM. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
